question: Vasco da Gama, who discovered the sea route from Europe to India, belonged to which nation?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Portugal**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Vasco da Gama, who discovered the sea route from Europe to India, belonged to **Portugal**.
 
• He was the first European to reach India by sea, linking Europe and Asia via the Cape of Good Hope.
 
• This discovery was significant as it opened the way for an age of global imperialism and for the Portuguese colonial empire to expand in Asia.
 
• Vasco da Gama's journey marked the beginning of a sea-based phase of global multiculturalism and trade.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Vasco da Gama's first voyage to India was from 1497 to 1499.
 
• He was appointed as the Portuguese viceroy in India in 1524 but died in Cochin (now Kochi) shortly after his arrival.
 
• His successful voyages helped establish a long-lasting colonial empire in Asia for Portugal.
 
• The sea route discovered by Vasco da Gama was instrumental in establishing Portuguese dominance in the Indian Ocean.
 
• His voyages paved the way for the Portuguese to establish a colonial empire in Asia, which included territories in India, Malacca, the Spice Islands, and Macau.
